Comment: Seed a Gutenberg subject and scrape every book it lists -- one execution takes a subject from a subject id to SCRAPED_HTML, announces that its books are ready, and ends. It does not standardize them, and does not wait for anything that does. Deployed as ${ENV_PREFIX}-scrape by the one ${ENV_PREFIX} stack (infra/resources.py, instantiated in infra/app.py), which shares its name with the scrape Lambda it calls -- legal, because a state machine ARN and a function ARN are different namespaces, but an alarm or a log filter has to say which of the two it means. The placeholders here are filled in by CDK definition_substitutions. See docs/operations.md, Orchestration.

list-subject-books.Comment: Creates a pipeline entry per book.

scrape-books.Comment: MaxConcurrency 1 paces gutenberg.org, a single volunteer-run host, and is also what makes the Wait states below a throttle rather than decoration: parallel iterations would overlap and the request rate would be whatever concurrency allowed.

throttle-metadata-scrape.Comment: Every gutenberg.org request is preceded by a pace, this one included, so the book boundary is throttled like any other request. Pacing before the fetch rather than after is what lets book-failed stay a Succeed: an iteration that ends early still cannot make the next book fetch immediately, because that book opens with its own pace.

scrape-content.Comment: Runs unconditionally: scrape_book_content guards on its own precondition and returns the book's existing status untouched, so a book that cannot advance -- non-English, or already at SCRAPED_HTML -- costs one read and no fetch. That guard is the only gate; a Choice here would be a second copy of it written against a status literal, which is exactly how this machine broke before.

book-failed.Comment: One book failing must not discard the rest of the subject, which is what an uncaught error in an inline Map would do. The book keeps its status, so the next run retries it; the error rides out in the Map result and is counted in `failed`.

books-to-standardize?.Comment: An empty book_ids is an ordinary outcome -- every book non-English, already standardized, or caught this run -- and not a refusal. Gating here keeps the announcement off that path, which is what lets the rule downstream match on detail-type alone: the event exists only when there is work. It also keeps the standardize machine off an input it would reject, since two falsy fields are neither of its entry points.

announce-books-scraped.Comment: Says that a subject's books reached SCRAPED_HTML, and ends. It does not say who should care: this machine names no ${ENV_PREFIX}-standardize-html anywhere, and a rule on the default bus is what turns this event into that machine's execution. book_ids rides in the event rather than being rediscovered downstream, which is what keeps the work list non-empty and BooksInFlightError meaningful -- EventBridge delivers at least once, so a duplicate event starts a second execution over books already at STANDARDIZE_SUBMITTED, and that refusal is what stops a second batch being paid for. A book an earlier run left at SCRAPED_HTML still comes back here, reported unchanged by scrape-content and kept by the filter without a refetch. What does strand a book is a caught error in this run: book-failed carries no status, so the filter drops it until the next run. See docs/operations.md, Orchestration, for the startExecution.sync:2 and download-ranking history this shape replaced.

announce-delivered?.Comment: PutEvents reports a rejected entry in FailedEntryCount and succeeds the task anyway, so without this the one failure that matters -- the event never reaching the bus -- reads as a finished subject that then silently never standardizes. Greater than zero rather than equal to one because Entries is a list.

announce-failed.Comment: The event did not reach the bus -- PutEvents raised, or accepted the call and rejected the entry. The scrape is already paid for and nothing downstream will hear that this subject has books waiting, so this is not a subject to report as done. No Retry above: a blind re-emit of an event that may in fact have been delivered starts a second standardize execution. The Error is a fixed name rather than the one that was caught, because a Fail state may not carry a reserved States.* name and an alarm needs something stable to key on; what was caught rides in the Cause. The ternary is what lets one Fail serve both ways in -- only the Catch above sets error and cause, so on the announce-delivered? path the count is the whole story.
announce-failed.Cause: {% $exists($states.input.error) ? $states.input.error & ': ' & $states.input.cause : 'PutEvents accepted the call and rejected the entry; FailedEntryCount ' & $string($states.input.failed_entries) %}

subject-done.Comment: The subject is scraped, and if any book reached SCRAPED_HTML the event saying so is on the bus. Not that it has been standardized, and not that anything acted on the event -- this machine has no way to know either, by design.
